title: Morning Market Briefing
context: Discussing market volatility and portfolio strategy during a morning investment committee meeting.
text: Good morning, everyone. As you saw in the pre-market, equities are taking a hit due to the new inflation data. We need to hedge our exposure immediately. I suggest we shift some capital into fixed income to weather the storm. Let's run the numbers and circle back before the closing bell.

Proposing a risk management or defensive strategy
Scheduling a follow-up discussion before the market closes

title: Ordering at the Corner Bakery
context: Mark is on his way to work and makes a quick stop at a busy bakery to grab breakfast before catching the subway.
text: Mark walked into the bakery with only five minutes to spare. The line was moving fast. When it was his turn, he smiled and said, 'Could I get that to go, please? I'm running a bit late for my train.' The cashier handed him a warm pastry and nodded, 'No problem at all! Have a great day ahead.' Mark grabbed his order and headed straight for the station.

title: Tight Layover at the Airport
context: Elena just landed in Chicago and has only 35 minutes to connect to her final flight to Seattle.
text: Elena rushed through Terminal 3, checking the flight monitors every few seconds. Her boarding pass showed gate B12, but the sign was flickering. She approached a gate agent and asked breathlessly, 'Excuse me, is this flight still boarding for Seattle? My connecting flight was delayed.' The agent checked her screen, 'Yes, they just announced final boarding. You're good to go!'

chunks.communicativeIntent: Checking if boarding doors are still open under time pressure

chunks.communicativeIntent: Explaining reason for late arrival concisely
chunks.connectedSpeech: Stress on 'delayed'; 'connecting flight' elides the final 'g'.

title: Describing Symptoms at the Walk-in Clinic
context: Clara visits an urgent care clinic after catching a bad cold during the winter season.
text: The nurse called Clara into room 4. Dr. Bennett walked in with a clipboard. 'Hello Clara, what seems to be the trouble today?' Clara cleared her throat gently, 'I've had this persistent cough for the past three days, and it feels worse whenever I lie down.' Dr. Bennett listened to her breathing, 'Your lungs sound clear, but let's make sure you get plenty of rest and stay hydrated.'

title: Polite Correction at a Dinner Gathering
context: Julian is having dinner with colleagues when the waiter brings a dish with an ingredient he specifically asked to avoid.
text: The waiter placed the plates across the table. Julian glanced down and noticed crushed peanuts on his salad. Instead of making a scene, he caught the waiter's eye discreetly. 'Excuse me, I'm terribly sorry, but I believe I ordered the garden salad without nuts due to an allergy.' The waiter was immediately apologetic, 'I am so sorry about that oversight. I'll have the kitchen remake that for you right away.'

chunks.communicativeIntent: Diplomatically correcting a mistake without blaming the person
Acknowledging a small unintended mistake professionally
